courses.name: Bachelor of Business Administration
courses.summary: The Bachelor of Business Administration is an undergraduate management degree taken after secondary school. Core study covers accounting, finance, marketing, organisational behaviour, human resource management, operations, business law and economics, usually followed by a specialisation such as business analytics, international business, digital marketing, finance or healthcare management, plus an internship or live project. Programmes run for three years in many systems and four years where an honours or research year is added. Graduates move into entry-level management roles or continue to an MBA or a specialist master's degree.

courses.name: M.E./M.Tech in Environmental Engineering
aliases: Master of Technology in Environmental Engineering
courses.summary: The M.E./M.Tech in Environmental Engineering is a postgraduate engineering degree for graduates in civil, chemical or environmental engineering or a related science. Advanced study covers water and wastewater treatment design, air-quality management, solid and hazardous waste engineering, environmental modelling, impact and risk assessment, and health and safety management, with a research dissertation in the final year. The degree normally lasts two years and leads to roles in environmental consultancy, pollution-control agencies, utilities and industry, or to doctoral research.

universities.name: Indian Maritime University
universities.summary: Indian Maritime University is a central university established by Parliament in 2008, headquartered in Chennai. Its six campuses teach maritime engineering, nautical science, naval architecture and logistics management in English. Entry varies by course, campus and applicant category; residential seagoing routes include medical standards and separate professional certification stages.
universities.campusLifestyle: IMU operates Chennai, Kochi, Kolkata, Mumbai Port, Navi Mumbai and Visakhapatnam campuses. Marine engineering and nautical programmes use residential study, while the listed management and technical master’s programmes are non-residential. Facilities and daily routines vary by teaching campus.
universities.cityProfile: IMU headquarters and its Chennai teaching campus are on East Coast Road at Semmencherry, Chennai. The university also teaches at Kochi, Kolkata, Mumbai Port, Navi Mumbai and Visakhapatnam. Check the campus on the allotment letter before planning accommodation or travel: a Chennai-headquartered university does not mean every course is taught in Chennai.
universities.practicalExposure: The university describes shipboard, workshop and simulator learning for marine engineering and nautical study. Naval architecture programmes focus on ship design and construction; the maritime logistics BBA has an apprenticeship component. Coursework, practical training, required sea service and professional competency certification are different stages. Admission or graduation does not guarantee a shipboard placement, licence or job.
universities.hostelOverview: Marine engineering, nautical science, DNS and the listed undergraduate naval architecture routes are residential; PGDME is residential too. Non-residential programmes may obtain campus accommodation only subject to availability and university discretion; hostel allocation is not a right.
universities.dietarySupport: The prospectus separates residential and non-residential charges and refers to accommodation and messing costs. Ask the allocated campus for its current mess arrangements, dietary requirements and complete charges before accepting accommodation.
universities.safetyOverview: IMU states a zero-tolerance policy on ragging, following UGC regulations and Supreme Court guidelines. Campus authorities are the stated reporting contact. Seagoing entry also requires the prescribed DG Shipping medical assessment.
universities.studentSupport: Admission includes counselling or a separate notified application route, document verification and medical certification. The university publishes programme-specific contacts, fee-withdrawal rules and foreign-admission guidance; use the contact for the chosen campus and route.

admissionsContent.overview: B.Tech. Marine Engineering at the Chennai Campus is a 4-year regular English programme. Residential engineering study in marine machinery and systems, with workshops, laboratory and simulator-based training.

eligibility.intro: The domestic entry requirements below apply to this campus programme. Foreign and other overseas categories need a separate programme-specific assessment.
items: 10+2 or equivalent with at least 60% average in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, and at least 50% in English at Class 10 or 12.
Maximum age on 1 August 2026: men General 25, OBC-NCL 28, SC/ST 30; women General 27, OBC-NCL 30, SC/ST 32. Applicants must be unmarried.

SC/ST: qualifying academic marks relax by 5 points. English relaxes by 5 only for native Lakshadweep/Andaman-Nicobar ST applicants where both parents also meet the specified island tribal birth/belonging conditions.
For the 2026 domestic UG route other than BBA, valid IMU-CET rank and percentile cutoff apply: General 60, EWS/OBC-NCL 54, SC/ST 45. These are test percentiles, separate from qualification marks.
Obtain physical fitness certification, including the prescribed vision and hearing assessment, from a DG Shipping-approved doctor. This is a residential programme.
The qualifying examination must meet the recognised-board and study-mode rules in section 13 of the prospectus; improvement subjects must come from the same board.

faq.question: Is Indian Maritime University a central university?
faq.answer: Yes. UGC lists IMU as a Central University established in 2008. The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways publishes its establishing Act. DG Shipping separately lists five maritime training campuses as approved; that does not mean every award is a seagoing licence.

faq.question: Where will I study?
faq.answer: Your course and allotment determine the campus. IMU has Chennai, Kochi, Kolkata, Mumbai Port, Navi Mumbai and Visakhapatnam campuses. Affiliated colleges are separately managed teaching institutions and are not the same as an IMU-owned campus.

faq.question: Are programmes taught in English?
faq.answer: Yes. IMU statutory ordinances specify English for the courses in its schools and affiliated institutions. The 2026-27 prospectus also explicitly states that its medium of instruction is English.

faq.question: What is the verified intake?
faq.answer: The 2026-27 regular programme calendar gives 1 August 2026 as commencement. This is a dated historical baseline. It does not announce future admission availability and is not extended here to online, new sustainability or research routes.

faq.question: Does every programme require IMU-CET?
faq.answer: No. Domestic seagoing undergraduate courses require IMU-CET and the current category percentile threshold. BBA uses Class 12 marks. MBA and M.Tech.have notified alternative entrance or merit routes; PGDME uses a separate Mumbai Port Campus process.

faq.question: What are the seagoing entry requirements?
faq.answer: The school-leaving route normally requires PCM60%and English 50%at Class 10 or 12, with exact programme-specific alternatives and relaxations. Age, unmarried status for the specified undergraduate courses and DG Shipping-approved medical certification apply. Read the exact programme entry conditions.

faq.question: Can overseas students apply?
faq.answer: The direct 2026-27 route lists two naval B.Tech.programmes at Visakhapatnam, BBA Logistics at Chennai, three specified M.Tech.routes and two MBA routes at Chennai. It uses separate academic, GRE/GMAT, age and equivalence conditions. DASA has separate rules; seagoing permission is not inferred.

faq.question: Which foreign tuition amount is confirmed?
faq.answer: Only the explicitly labelled 2026-27 non-residential SAARC/BIMSTEC/African-country tuition is quoted where the direct campus route is verified: INR175,000 annually for the listed MBA/M.Tech.or INR75,000 for Chennai BBA. This is a regional category quote, with other charges extra; it does not cover all international applicants.

faq.question: Why are some fees on request?
faq.answer: Costs depend on the programme, campus, admission route and nationality classification. Request a written quotation that separates tuition from programme and registration fees, deposits, hostel, mess and other compulsory costs. Compare the complete budget before accepting a place.

faq.question: Is hostel accommodation guaranteed?
faq.answer: The specified residential programmes require campus residence. For non-residential courses, accommodation is subject to availability and university discretion. Confirm hostel and mess arrangements and charges with the allocated campus.

faq.question: Does the DNS diploma complete a bachelor’s degree in one year?
faq.answer: No. The one-year Diploma in Nautical Science is a pre-sea stage leading towards B.Sc.Applied Nautical Science. Required subsequent training, sea service and examinations are separate; do not treat the diploma alone as a completed bachelor’s degree.

faq.question: Does completing the course guarantee employment or a licence?
faq.answer: No. University study, required professional training, sea service and competency certification are distinct. Admission, graduation or an apprenticeship component does not guarantee permanent employment, shipboard placement or a professional licence.

faq.question: How do I apply and plan documents?
faq.answer: Use the currentIMUadmission notice for your programme and route, select the exact campus and complete counselling or separate application, allotment and original-document verification. Prepare academic, entrance, age/category and medical records as applicable. Foreign applicants also need equivalence and immigration documentation.

IMU operates Chennai, Kochi, Kolkata, Mumbai Port, Navi Mumbai and Visakhapatnam campuses. Marine engineering and nautical programmes use residential study, while the listed management and technical master’s programmes are non-residential. Facilities and daily routines vary by teaching campus.

IMU headquarters and its Chennai teaching campus are on East Coast Road at Semmencherry, Chennai. The university also teaches at Kochi, Kolkata, Mumbai Port, Navi Mumbai and Visakhapatnam. Check the campus on the allotment letter before planning accommodation or travel: a Chennai-headquartered university does not mean every course is taught in Chennai.

The university describes shipboard, workshop and simulator learning for marine engineering and nautical study. Naval architecture programmes focus on ship design and construction; the maritime logistics BBA has an apprenticeship component. Coursework, practical training, required sea service and professional competency certification are different stages. Admission or graduation does not guarantee a shipboard placement, licence or job.

Marine engineering, nautical science, DNS and the listed undergraduate naval architecture routes are residential; PGDME is residential too. Non-residential programmes may obtain campus accommodation only subject to availability and university discretion; hostel allocation is not a right.

The prospectus separates residential and non-residential charges and refers to accommodation and messing costs. Ask the allocated campus for its current mess arrangements, dietary requirements and complete charges before accepting accommodation.

IMU states a zero-tolerance policy on ragging, following UGC regulations and Supreme Court guidelines. Campus authorities are the stated reporting contact. Seagoing entry also requires the prescribed DG Shipping medical assessment.

Admission includes counselling or a separate notified application route, document verification and medical certification. The university publishes programme-specific contacts, fee-withdrawal rules and foreign-admission guidance; use the contact for the chosen campus and route.
